summary: Norfolk County, MA municipal 40-ft steel tower on Grossman Camp Hill, used 1930 to 1955; the register says it still stands, which conflicts with our 'gone' status.

facts.status_note: The register says it is still standing; no second source we read confirms its condition

events.note: First operated in 1930 per the register; the register gives no build date
Registered September 3, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

evidence.supports: 40-foot steel tower, first operated 1930, used until 1955
evidence.quote: This 40' steel tower was first operated in 1930 and was used until 1955.

evidence.supports: municipal tower; register says still standing
evidence.quote: This tower was a municipal tower and is still standing.

evidence.supports: the sheet lists Massachusetts fire towers
the sheet lists the site as Westwood - Grossman Camp Hill

corrections.why: The register says the municipal tower is still standing; no other source we read confirms or contradicts this

notes_for_editor: The register is the only source for the tower's history, and it says still standing and municipal. The brief said gone. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Massachusetts Facebook post, seen only in search results, also says still standing and gives 1930 to 1955, but the page did not load, so it is not cited. The Red Knights sheet is an undated pin checklist, so it is not evidence of current condition. No access information was found. Ask a human to check Westwood town records or a recent visit before changing the status.
